subject: Opsync pilot: econ packaging & quant/batching technical handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@opsync.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring Optimize toolkit pricing for Opsync pilot

Hi Vivek / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Opsync is evaluating a 3-month pilot to validate vector search + generation at scale for customer support summarization. A few asks up front so we can scope the pilot and discuss pricing: 

- Typical workload: ~120k requests/day, average prompt+completion tokens ≈ 420, 95th pct request length ~1,200 tokens.
- Latency expectation: p95 under 350ms for generate calls (we can relax to 500ms if batching helps cost).
- Security: must run in hosted mode with committed region in us-west.

We're particularly interested in Redwood's Optimize toolkit: batching and KV cache guidance, and recommended quantization level for our throughput (we'll likely test int8 / GPTQ). From a commercial perspective, Opsync needs a modest pilot credit and a path to a committed discount if we convert. 

Attached: opsync-RFP.pdf (high level). Can we set a plan and an initial credit proposal this week?

Cheers,
Jordan
Head of Product, Opsync

Attachments: opsync-RFP.pdf (pdf, 1 page)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@opsync.io>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Optimize toolkit pricing for Opsync pilot

Jordan — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP. Quick notes and next steps: 

1) We can put together a two-track pilot: (A) cost-focused: maximize savings via batching + KV caching and an Optimize credits pool, and (B) latency-focused: a lower-latency config with smaller batch windows.
2) To size credits and recommend quantization we need: sample traffic distribution (per-second request histogram), token distribution (prompt vs completion), and any hard latency SLOs per API route.
3) Recommend a 60–90 minute technical handoff between Camila / Priyom and your infra/ML lead so we can propose concrete knobs (batch size, max wait, KV cache TTL, quantization profile).

Can you send the workload sample and propose times? I'll put together an initial pilot credit framework to propose back.

— Vivek
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — inference@redwood.com
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@opsync.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, procurement@opsync.io
Date: 2027-06-13T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Optimize toolkit pricing for Opsync pilot

Thanks Vivek — attaching the sample workload and a short histogram file.

Highlights:
- Peak: 3x baseline between 14:00–17:00 PST (we see ~1.1k rps peak seconds but average sustained is ~32 rps).
- Prompt vs completion split: 30% prompt tokens, 70% completion tokens.
- Typical model: open-architecture 70B family (we're open to alternatives if you recommend lower-context variants).

We'd like an initial commercial play: $15k in pilot credits + a 12% first-year discount on committed usage if we sign within 60 days. Procurement is on cc; they asked for a short MAP (mutual action plan) and a term sheet preview.

Attached: opsync-workload-sample.csv

Jordan
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@opsync.io>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-13T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Optimize toolkit pricing for Opsync pilot — technical recommendations

Jordan — quick technical runbook based on what you shared. High-level recommendations (we'll go deeper in the handoff):

- Model choice: Start with a 70B variant compiled for int8 (GPTQ) as a middle ground. If quality loss shows, we can lift to int16 for top-of-funnel generation.
- Batching: target dynamic batching with a 5–12ms max-wait for p50-sensitive routes; allow up to 30ms max-wait on bulk/generation routes to accumulate efficient batches. Given your p95 target we can use a 12ms window as default for generate endpoints.
- KV cache: enable prefix KV caching for common customer prompts (TTL 10–20m). Expect 25–40% token savings for repeated flows; we should instrument hit-rate in week 1.
- Quantization caveats: GPTQ gives large cost wins but can introduce brittle tokenization artifacts for long-tail prompts. We'll run an A/B set over sampled traffic.

Commercially: based on your profile I'd propose:
- Pilot: $10k Redwood Optimize credits (covers runtime + Optimize consulting) + 30 hours of SE time for tuning and two workshops.
- Conversion: tiered discount ladder: 8% at $X/mo commit, 12% at $Y/mo commit, with a one-time migration credit if you sign a 12-month reserved capacity contract.

I'm attaching a draft MAP for your procurement to review. If Opsync can commit to a short handoff this week, Priyom and I will finalize quantization profiles and a 2-week A/B plan.

Thanks,
Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-opsync-draft.docx (docx, 2 pages)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@opsync.io>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, procurement@opsync.io
Date: 2027-06-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Opsync pilot: econ packaging & quant/batching technical handoff

Jordan / Procurement team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary + counter-proposal so we have a single doc to move to signatures: 

Executive summary:
- We propose a 6-week pilot: 2 weeks for instrumentation/traffic mirroring + quant A/B, 4 weeks for production-like testing.
- Pilot commercial: Redwood will provide $12,500 in Optimize credits (runtime + SE time), plus up to 40 hours of SE support (Camila / Priyom).
- Conversion pathway: if Opsync executes a 12-month reserved capacity contract within 60 days we will apply an early-conversion credit equal to 25% of pilot credits and a first-year discount of 10%. We can tier deeper discounts at higher commit bands — Camila included the ladder in the MAP.

Technical trade-offs and rationale:
- We endorse Camila's int8/GPTQ-first approach with clear rollback to int16 for any quality regression > 1.5% on your eval set.
- Given your peak/sustained profile, autoscaling + KV cache gives the best cost/latency mix versus overprovisioning a low-latency pool. We'll instrument p95 during the pilot and allow a single fallback to a dedicated lower-latency pool for burst windows if needed (this would be billable on usage above committed thresholds).

Next steps (recommended):
1) Opsync procurement signs an initial Pilot Term Sheet (preview attached).
2) We schedule a 90-minute technical handoff (Camila / Priyom + Opsync infra/ML) by EOD Wednesday.
3) Redwood SEs run a baseline eval on the sample workload and deliver a quantification report within 5 business days of handoff.

Links & attachments:
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/OPS-2027-042
- Term sheet preview (attached): term-sheet-preview.pdf
- DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/OPS-TS-042

Jordan — does this bridge expectations? If yes we'll send a short Pilot Term Sheet to procurement for signature and block the handoff slots.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — www.redwood.ai
